conventions.convention: Use R(X,Y)Z = ∇X∇Y Z − ∇Y∇X Z − ∇[X,Y]Z and the Jacobi equation D_t²J + R(J,T)T = 0; the geodesic parameter in the variation/Jacobi results is affine.
For an oriented surface, J is the positive quarter-turn, and the oriented orthonormal frame has ω(X) = g(∇X E1,E2), ∇E1 = ωE2, ∇E2 = −ωE1; therefore dω = −K dA and a rotation gives ω′ = ω + dφ.

The signed geodesic curvature is kg = g(∇T T, JT); boundary orientation is outward-normal-first; at an ordinary corner the signed exterior angle is π minus the interior angle, with no cusp or antipodal tangent.
For a supplied finite triangulation, χ is the alternating count V − E + F; the surface theorem uses it only after proving independence from the supplied triangulation and metric.

Characteristic forms use c(∇) = det(I − Ω/(2πi)), p_j(∇) = (−1)^j c_{2j}(∇C), and e(∇) = Pf(Ω/(2π)) in an ordered oriented orthonormal frame with Pf([[0,a],[-a,0]]) = a. First Chern class of a complex line is the Euler class of its complex-oriented real plane.
The cut-locus volume statement uses the Borel Radon measure induced by the Riemannian density; it does not take a completion, and the closed cut locus is Borel.

The cut-locus volume theorem states ACω and assumes a complete, connected, boundaryless finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold with a point; the finite geodesic triangulation construction assumes full AC.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. If M is either (a) a compact regular oriented surface region with finitely many ordinary corners inside an oriented boundaryless Riemannian surface, with g the restricted metric, or (b) a compact oriented smooth surface with smooth boundary with its metric-extension open neighbourhood in the smooth double supplied, then ∫M K dA + ∫∂M kg ds + Σj αj = 2πχ(M), with the corner sum empty in (b) and both boundary terms omitted when ∂M is empty.

Assume full AC. For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle with a Hermitian metric and Hermitian connection, J([c_j(∇)]) = ρ(c_j(E)) for every j ≥ 0; for every finite-rank smooth real bundle with any real connection D, J([p_j(D)]) = ρ(p_j(V)); for every oriented Euclidean bundle of even rank with a metric-compatible connection, J([e(∇)]) = ρ(e(W)).

For any two compatible connections on the same supplied G-reduction, the Chern–Weil classes agree; for every smooth map f, the class of the pulled-back bundle and connection is the pullback of the original class. Under full AC, every bundle with a fixed GL, U, or SO reduction in the stated scope admits a compatible connection.
Under full AC, for a compact oriented closed Riemannian surface (M,g), ∫M K dA = 2πχ(M).

Assume ACω. For a complete, connected, boundaryless, finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold (M,g) and p ∈ M, the cut locus Cut(p) has zero Riemannian volume; no compactness or total-volume hypothesis is assumed.
Under ACω, on a complete connected boundaryless finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, c_p(u) > 0 and c_p is continuous as a map S_pM → (0,+∞] with the order topology.

Assume full AC. In the supplied compact smooth-boundary or regular cornered surface-region setting, there is a finite face-to-face triangulation retaining the prescribed boundary arcs and corners, with nonboundary edges regular C² geodesic embeddings.

concerns.concern: In proof 1.1, s_u(t) = cos(t/R)p + R sin(t/R)u is differentiated as s′_u(t) = −sin(t/R)p + R cos(t/R)u. The actual derivative is −(1/R)sin(t/R)p + cos(t/R)u. The printed derivative has the wrong coefficients and gives speed squared sin²(t/R) + R²cos²(t/R), not 1 except when R = 1; the proof’s unit-speed computation is false as written.

Proof 3.1 says “Since c(u_n)<t, step 1.1 gives d_g(p,q_n)<t,” but step 1.1 proves equality only for times t < c(u_n), so it does not apply in this direction. From c(u_n)<t, the definition of c as a supremum gives that t is not minimizing; the radial path has length t, so d_g(p,q_n) ≤ t and hence d_g(p,q_n) < t. This is a short gap that can be closed from the definition.

Proof 1.2 claims that for merely C² boundary germs, the angular graph has α′(r) = c + o(1) and rα″(r) → 0, then says the inverse corner straightening makes every pulled-back regular C² edge have a continuous second derivative at the corner. The latter does not follow: for α₋(r)=0 and α₊(r)=θ₀+r^(7/2)sin(1/r), rα₊″(r)→0 and the corresponding boundary germ is C², but the inverse angle of an interior straight ray, β(r)=πθ/[θ₀+r^(7/2)sin(1/r)], has an unbounded second derivative near 0. Thus the stated C² corner construction is unsupported under the given regularity without a stronger hypothesis or a different construction.

seams_checked.note: The classification page states that every nonempty compact connected boundaryless topological 2-manifold is exactly one of the sphere, a connected sum of tori, or a connected sum of projective planes, and that orientability plus Euler characteristic classifies homeomorphism type. The Gauss–Bonnet page says only that classification is needed to infer genus, normal form, or homeomorphism type and is not proved or used there. This summarizes the theorem’s role rather than stating its proposition, so the seam is not textually faithful under the task’s citation-fidelity rule.
